claim: Nikon Type F immersion oil, part MXA22168, has a refractive index ne of 1.515 at 23 degrees Celsius, as published by the reseller Morrell Instrument Company.

numbers.name: refractive_index
numbers.note: printed as 'Index ne(23 degrees C)=1.515'. No wavelength in figures; ne is the mercury e line, 546.1 nm, by notation.

identifiers.product: Nikon Type F Non-Fluorescing Immersion Oil

validity_conditions: A TYPE FACT ABOUT THE PRODUCT, published by a reseller and not by Nikon, found while searching for Nikon's own Type F sheet, which was not found (src_edmund_57189_nikon_type_f_page lists what was searched). It reaches this bench only through immersion_oil_in_use_is_nikon_type_f. The catalogue number is the page's and Nikon's safety sheet's for Type F 30 cc; it was not read off the bench's bottle, so it identifies the product and not the bottle. THE WAVELENGTH IS NOTATION: the page prints 'ne' and no figure, and validity pins 546.1 nm because that is what the subscript e means. The temperature is the page's own, 23 degC, pinned at 296.15 K. Point validity in both, so a query at another wavelength is no_overlap and nothing is interpolated. DISPERSION: the page prints ve(23 degC) = 40.8, kept verbatim in the source record and not entered, because no dispersion quantity is registered. IN CONFLICT WITH nikon_type_f_oil_refractive_index_nd_23c (rule 7, both kept): that reseller gives nd(23 degC) = 1.518. For an oil of normal dispersion ne at 546.1 nm is not lower than nd at 587.6 nm, so 1.515 and 1.518 cannot both be right as labelled; nothing reachable here settles which page has it wrong. NOT A LIMIT: an optical property of the oil, and no envelope value derives from it.
